title: A Inheritance for the Confession
premise: Retired detective Xanthe Villalobos receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a seven-year-old drowning ruled accidental, and one unsigned, promising 'more if you find the ledger.' The confession is written in her late husband's handwriting — though he died before the crime. As Xanthe decodes an accounting ledger hidden in her bookshop's rare first editions, she uncovers that her husband, the town's beloved sheriff, covered up the drowning of a young woman to protect his deputy brother, and spent his final years trying to confess. When the statute of limitations nears expiry, the true killer — now the town's mayor — moves to destroy the evidence and silence anyone who remembers. In the end, Xanthe must choose between preserving her husband's posthumous reputation and delivering justice outside the law: she publishes the decoded ledger publicly on the statute's last day, letting the town itself render its verdict.
about_author: Edmund Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent fifteen years filing confessions that never made it to trial. He writes mysteries from a converted records office in coastal Maine, where he still alphabetizes everything.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Xanthe opens her failing bookshop on a rain-slicked Tuesday and finds twin letters: a signed confession to manslaughter from her dead husband, and an anonymous note promising 'more if you find the ledger.' Her POV establishes grief sharpened into suspicion. The emotional beat is vertigo — seven years of mourning destabilized by a single line of familiar handwriting.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Xanthe rereads her husband's old case files at night, discovering the drowned woman, Marisol Reyes, was ruled accidental despite missing shoes. POV alternates with Marisol's sister, Luz, who returns to town asking quiet questions. The beat is dread: two investigations converging on the same wound neither woman can name yet.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Xanthe notices pencil marks in the margins of her husband's donated first editions — numbers matching ledger columns. She realizes the bookshop itself is the hiding place. The mayor, Dale Corven, visits the shop for the first time in years, all charm and warning. Beat: the hunter realizes she is also being hunted.

chapters.title: What the Deputy Knew
chapters.summary: Luz tracks down the retired deputy brother, Emmett, now dying in a care home, who half-confesses he was on the dock that night but swears he didn't push her. His terror isn't of prison but of Corven. Xanthe's POV; the beat is pity curdling into resolve as she sees how fear was administered for years.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: A lawyer confirms the window closes in nineteen days. Xanthe accelerates decoding while someone breaks into the shop overnight, rifling the rare books but taking nothing — they don't know which volume yet. Luz's POV reveals she received an identical anonymous letter. Beat: alliance formed between the widow and the sister.

chapters.title: Entries in Red
chapters.summary: Decoded pages reveal payments: Corven's campaign funded by the family whose son was in the boat that night. Xanthe confronts the possibility her husband took hush money too — or was documenting it. Flashback chapter in his voice via journal fragments. Beat: love against duty, as she refuses to stop even if it damns him.

chapters.title: Fire in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Arson guts the back room of the bookshop; the rare editions survive only because Xanthe moved them days earlier, sensing the pattern. A fire marshal's report is quietly buried. Emmett dies the same night — officially natural causes. Beat: escalation; the enemy has stopped pretending, and Xanthe stops trusting institutions entirely.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: The final ledger page, hidden in her husband's personal Bible, names the killer outright: not the boy in the boat, but Corven himself, who followed them to the dock. It also contains her husband's full confession of the cover-up, written to be found by her. Beat: climax of memory — she must decide what truth costs.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Corven offers Xanthe the shop's mortgage free and clear in exchange for the ledger. She lets him believe she accepted, then scans every page. On the statute's final day, she and Luz distribute copies at the courthouse steps, the diner, the church. Beat: justice outside the law — no arrest possible, only exposure.

chapters.title: Shelved Under R
chapters.summary: Corven resigns under weight of the town's verdict; a grand jury convenes anyway on new evidence. Xanthe reopens the shop, shelving the decoded ledger beside her husband's letters under 'R' for Reyes — public record at last. Luz stays in town. Final beat: love against duty resolved — she loved him enough to tell the truth about him.
